activity_statements.statement: operates T-Mobile US as its largest segment, providing postpaid and prepaid mobile services to 129.5 million US customers (104.1M postpaid) with FY2024 service revenues of $66.1B
provides fixed-line broadband, fiber/FTTH, mobile, and IPTV (4.6M TV subscribers) services to consumers and businesses in Germany under the Telekom brand
operates mobile and fixed-line telecom services across multiple European countries, generating €12.3B in revenue in FY2024
delivers enterprise IT and digital transformation services through T-Systems, including AI-enabled supply chain solutions, with €4.0B revenue and €4.0B order entry in FY2024
generates €115.8B total group revenue (FY2024), with 79% from international operations, operating in 50+ countries
is expanding its fiber network infrastructure in Germany and acquiring European fiber network operators (e.g., Fiberhost and Inea from Macquarie) to build FTTH coverage
is building a 5G campus network for automated port operations, providing private 5G network deployment services for industrial customers

name_reality_gap: Listed as a German 'Telecommunications' company; nearly two-thirds of its revenue comes from T-Mobile US, making it de facto one of the largest US wireless carriers — Deutsche Telekom is primarily an American mobile business that also owns German and European telecom assets.
extraction_notes: Strong segment data available from 2024 annual report press release. T-Mobile US segment weight calculated from USD revenue converted to share of group EUR total. T-Systems weight reflects its €4.0B vs €115.8B group revenue.
